_comment: Shared golden vectors for the year heat-map's drawing window. Loaded by BOTH
suites: YearGridVectorTest.swift drives PotillusKit's YearGrid.isDrawn, and
The rule is the one thing the year view has that the month view does not: a
day after the logical today is the future, and a day before the statistics
start date is in the span the user excluded from every statistic. Both are
drawn as nothing at all, because a neutral cell is what an ABSTINENT day
gets and using it here would claim something no entry supports.
Dates are `yyyy-MM-dd` and are compared as STRINGS on both platforms — the
format is fixed-width and zero-padded, so lexical order is chronological.
statsFrom null means no statistics start date is set.
The boundaries are the point of this file: `today` itself IS drawn, the
start date itself IS drawn, and the day either side of them is not. Both
bounds are inclusive; a strict comparison on one platform and a
non-strict one on the other is exactly the drift this pins.

isDrawn.description: a day inside the window with no floor
a later month of the same year is the future
the start date itself is drawn
the day before the start date is excluded
the day after the start date is drawn
the whole previous year is excluded by the floor
a fresh install: the start date is today, so only today is drawn
a fresh install: yesterday falls outside the floor
both bounds bite: after today and before the floor cannot both hold, so the future wins
29 February of a leap year is an ordinary day inside the window
